pr.title: feat(etag): allow for custom hashing methods to be used to etag

summary: This PR adds an optional `generateDigest` option to the etag middleware, threading a hashing function through to `digest.ts`'s `generateDigest`, defaulting to SHA-1 (same as before) — this part is backward compatible and covered by a new test. However, the diff also silently removes the `await c.res.blob() // Force using body` line from the 304 branch, which is unrelated to the stated feature and undocumented in the PR description; this line existed specifically to force full consumption of the original response's body stream before discarding it in favor of the new 304 Response, and removing it could reintroduce resource/stream-consumption issues in some runtimes even though existing tests still pass. Additionally, `generateDigest`'s exported signature changed to require a new `generator` parameter, which is a minor internal API contract change worth double-checking against any external usage.

findings.rationale: The line `await c.res.blob() // Force using body` was removed in the same PR as the etag hashing feature, with no mention in the PR description explaining why. This line forced full consumption of the pre-304 response body stream before c.res was replaced. Removing it is unrelated to the stated feature and could reintroduce dangling/unconsumed ReadableStream issues on some runtimes (e.g. warnings or resource leaks), which existing unit tests would not catch since they only assert header/body contents, not stream lifecycle.
findings.suggestedCheck: Confirm with git blame/history why this line was originally added (likely to avoid a warning/leak about unconsumed streams) and verify removing it doesn't reintroduce that issue on Node/Bun/Deno/CF Workers runtimes, especially for streamed responses.

findings.rationale: generateDigest's exported function signature changed (added required `generator` param). It's used internally only by etag/index.ts, so no external callers appear broken, but if this module is re-exported or imported elsewhere (e.g. from a public entrypoint), it would be a breaking change.
findings.suggestedCheck: Verify digest.ts is not part of any public export surface (package.json exports/subpath) that third-party code might import directly.
